card.name: Start of capitalized medical abbreviations
card.fires_on: The first letter (H or S) of an acronym for a condition in parentheses, such as HPP, HSTCL, HUS/TTP or HITT. Also the S that starts 'Sepsis' after an infection percentage.

modes.label: Condition acronyms
modes.description: The opening H of an uppercase abbreviation for a disease or syndrome, often right after an open parenthesis.
modes.example: thrombocytopenia and hemolytic uremic syndrome/thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (<<H>>US/TTP)

modes.label: Sepsis after pneumonia rates
modes.description: The S that begins the sentence 'Sepsis occurred in' right after a pneumonia percentage.
modes.example: Pneumonia occurred in 21% of patients, with Grade 3 or 4 occurring in 15%.<< S>>epsis occurred in 14%

card.writes: It boosts word starts like 'h' and 'hem', which suggests it helps spell out words that begin with h.
card.plain: It fires on the first letter of a disease abbreviation or of 'Sepsis' in warning-style label text.
